# Adaptate

> Typed, validated data from OpenAPI, JSON Schema, or Zod, including JSON that is still streaming.

# Docs

Source: docs/index.md

---
title: "Docs"
description: "Typed, validated data from OpenAPI, JSON Schema, or Zod, including JSON that is still streaming."
answer: "Install adaptate, turn an OpenAPI or JSON Schema into Zod, and check data against it, including a tool call that is still streaming. Each view can require only its own fields."
faq:
  - question: "Which package do I install?"
    answer: "adaptate for transformSchema, @adaptate/utils for OpenAPI, and @adaptate/core when you need the /stream, /verify, /standard, or /effect subpaths. zod is a peer. @adaptate/accel, @adaptate/wasm, and @adaptate/native are optional Advanced packages, not part of the default zero-dep install."
  - question: "Is the API reference generated?"
    answer: "Yes. pnpm docs:api writes docs/api from the .d.ts files that ship in @adaptate/core and @adaptate/utils."
---

# Docs

## Install

```sh
npm i adaptate @adaptate/utils zod
```

`adaptate` ships the root entry of `@adaptate/core`. Install `@adaptate/core` instead when you import a subpath such as `@adaptate/core/stream` or `@adaptate/core/verify`. The default install stays zero-dependency aside from the `zod` peer.

## Quick start

An OpenAPI or JSON Schema object becomes a Zod schema:

```ts
import { openAPISchemaToZod } from "@adaptate/utils";

const recipe = openAPISchemaToZod({
  type: "object",
  required: ["title"],
  properties: {
    title: { type: "string" },
    servings: { type: "integer" },
  },
});
recipe.safeParse({ title: "Pasta", servings: 4 }).success; // true
```

One Zod schema, and a card that requires only the title:

```ts
import { z } from "zod";
import { transformSchema, type Config } from "adaptate";

const recipe = z.object({ title: z.string(), servings: z.number() });
type Recipe = z.infer<typeof recipe>;
const card = { title: true } satisfies Config<Recipe>;
const cardSchema = transformSchema(recipe.partial(), card);
cardSchema.parse({ title: "Pasta" });
```

Agents can read [llms.txt](../llms.txt) for an index, or [llms-full.txt](../llms-full.txt) for every page.

## Guides

- [Transform](transform.md): one Zod schema, and a config that marks which fields each screen requires.
- [Streaming](streaming.md): check a tool call while the JSON is still arriving.
- [v3 feeds](v3.md): a `makeFeed` hook on stream steps, with `openPath` and `tailOpen` unchanged.
- [AG-UI](ag-ui.md): check AG-UI tool-call deltas against each view.
- [Web streams](web-streams.md): feed a ReadableStream, SSE, or a Node stream into the parser.
- [OpenAPI](openapi.md): turn an OpenAPI schema into Zod, and write a Zod schema back out.
- [Zod](zod.md): one Zod schema, a `Config` per view, and the Standard Schema interface.
- [Effect](effect.md): run the same checks in an Effect pipeline.
- [Find your choke points](choke-points.md): parse to an ok or error track, then map, flatMap, or recover.
- [TypeScript](typescript.md): types ship in the package and are checked on TypeScript 7 and 6.
- [Subpaths](subpaths.md): the published entry points, and which peers each one loads.
- [Optional peers](optional-peers.md): effect, js-yaml, and the ref parser load only when that code is imported.
- [Acceleration](accel.md): optional native, WASM, and GPU packages for large buffers, plus a live JS vs WASM benchmark.
- [Runtime verification](verification.md): fail-closed in-memory hooks before any write to disk.
- [Migration 2.4](migration-2.4.md): YAML and the ref parser became optional peers.
- [Migration 3.0](migration-3.0.md): additive `makeFeed`, `@adaptate/core/verify`, and optional acceleration packages.
- [Development](development.md): install, test, and build this repository.

## API

- [API reference](api/index.md): generated from the `.d.ts` files that ship in the packages.


# The adaptate journey

Source: JOURNEY.md

# The adaptate journey

The problem started at Oneflow, where entity schemas did not match across endpoints while I was building features. I wrote the precursor by hand, alone. I wanted to open-source it back then; it didn't happen. After I lost access to the code (nothing secret was kept), I rebuilt adaptate from general programming concepts — recursion and mutual recursion. No Oneflow code is in adaptate.

```mermaid
timeline
    title adaptate
    2 Nov 2024 : First commit
    4 Nov 2024 : ChatGPT share in the README : First npm publish
    6 Nov 2024 : Monorepo split : @adaptate/core on npm
    5 May 2026 : Cursor Agent in git : OIDC trusted publishing
    11 May 2026 : Grok noted in pull request 21
    21 Nov 2026 : Streaming partial parser
    22 Nov 2026 : Iterative walks : 2.4.0
```

## Origin

This repository starts at the [initial commit](https://github.com/p10ns11y/adaptate/commit/f506830ac98a4e8b2a2629c97585eb31bc0acabb) on 2 Nov 2024, then [the first source](https://github.com/p10ns11y/adaptate/commit/2999c5815226b3b6810f3a0784b81057b5f4d7e1) the next day. That first source walks Zod objects recursively.

## Rebuild

A [ChatGPT Canvas share](https://chatgpt.com/share/6728eb4e-07f8-8005-b586-c4b8ee0e798c) was added to the README on 4 Nov 2024, in [the v0.0.3 commit](https://github.com/p10ns11y/adaptate/commit/c3721c0f1f2aa515e66e38525db63a563283bad5) that also fixed edge cases and grew the tests. The same share stayed in the README through [v2.0.0](https://github.com/p10ns11y/adaptate/commit/ce1947bddf977479ffc2efd81fea0546e0b5a306). That README recorded that the prototype used `.required()` where `.unwrap()` was needed, and that this was corrected by hand.

The share link was removed on 11 May 2026, in [the #21 work](https://github.com/p10ns11y/adaptate/pull/21) ([7e1c611](https://github.com/p10ns11y/adaptate/commit/7e1c611614d73a98d1f8b3032c8551a44776baea)).

## Publish

The first npm publish was [`adaptate@0.1.0`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/adaptate/v/0.1.0) on 4 Nov 2024. [`adaptate@0.0.1`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/adaptate/v/0.0.1) followed later that day. The monorepo split is [a49a375](https://github.com/p10ns11y/adaptate/commit/a49a3752ee6c4a5cd63d60e7c8506cf159f2a70c) on 6 Nov 2024; [`@adaptate/core@0.0.7`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@adaptate/core/v/0.0.7) was published that evening.

## Cursor, Grok, and 2.4

[Cursor Agent](https://github.com/p10ns11y/adaptate/commit/395cfb1f7182d8aeea4da7edbf3f997f4e2cc267) first appears in git on 5 May 2026. The same day brought [OIDC trusted publishing](https://github.com/p10ns11y/adaptate/commit/e9a15d6c48c3ebc143a982648b73d15e6032ba69) ([#17](https://github.com/p10ns11y/adaptate/pull/17), then [#19](https://github.com/p10ns11y/adaptate/pull/19) and [#20](https://github.com/p10ns11y/adaptate/pull/20)), later hardened in [#31](https://github.com/p10ns11y/adaptate/pull/31). [#21](https://github.com/p10ns11y/adaptate/pull/21) is where the project first recorded Grok as an agent on the work.

Streaming partial validation landed in [#48](https://github.com/p10ns11y/adaptate/pull/48) on 21 Nov 2026. On 22 Nov 2026, [#66](https://github.com/p10ns11y/adaptate/pull/66) replaced unbounded recursive walks with explicit stacks, and [#69](https://github.com/p10ns11y/adaptate/pull/69) cut [v2.4.0](https://github.com/p10ns11y/adaptate/releases/tag/v2.4.0).


# Transform

Source: docs/transform.md

---
title: "Transform"
description: "One Zod schema, and a config that marks which fields each screen requires."
answer: "transformSchema(schema, config) returns a Zod schema where the fields marked true in the config are required. Fields the config does not mention keep their original optionality."
faq:
  - question: "What does transformSchema return?"
    answer: "A Zod schema. The configured fields are required and every other field stays as it was."
  - question: "How do I require a field on every array item?"
    answer: "Use the '*' key, for example { tags: { '*': true } }."
  - question: "How do I require a field only in some cases?"
    answer: "Use makeConditionalSchemaTransformer(data)(schema, config) with requiredIf: (data) => boolean."
---

# Transform

`transformSchema(schema, config)` returns a Zod schema with the configured fields required. Unmentioned fields stay as they were.

Config values:

- `true` — strip optionality
- `false` — keep the field optional
- nested object — recurse
- `{ '*': config }` — apply `config` to each array element
- `(data) => boolean` or `{ requiredIf: (data) => boolean }` — with `makeConditionalSchemaTransformer` only

```ts
import { z } from "zod";
import { transformSchema, type Config } from "@adaptate/core";

const schema = z.deepPartial(
  z.object({
    name: z.string(),
    age: z.number(),
    address: z.object({
      street: z.string(),
      city: z.string(),
    }),
  }),
);

const config = {
  name: true,
  age: true,
  address: { city: true },
} satisfies Config<z.infer<typeof schema>>;

const updatedSchema = transformSchema(schema, config);
updatedSchema.parse({ name: "Davin", age: 30, address: { city: "Pettit" } });
const streetOnly = updatedSchema.safeParse({
  name: "Davin",
  age: 30,
  address: { street: "Main St" },
});
```

`streetOnly.success` is false: `city` is required.

Zod 4 exports `z.deepPartial`. The object method `.deepPartial()` is the Zod 3 method. The same config works when each field is written with `.optional()` instead of `z.deepPartial`.

`Config<T>` checks field paths at compile time, including `'*'` on arrays:

```ts
import { z } from "zod";
import { type Config } from "@adaptate/core";

const userSchema = z.object({
  name: z.string(),
  address: z.object({ street: z.string(), city: z.string() }),
  tags: z.array(z.string()),
});

const config = {
  name: true,
  address: { city: true },
  tags: { "*": true },
} satisfies Config<z.infer<typeof userSchema>>;
```

`makeConditionalSchemaTransformer(data)(schema, config)` applies `requiredIf` against that `data`.

```ts
import { z } from "zod";
import { makeConditionalSchemaTransformer } from "@adaptate/core";

const schema = z.object({
  parentContactNumber: z.number().optional(),
  age: z.number().optional(),
});
const config = {
  parentContactNumber: { requiredIf: (data: { age?: number }) => (data.age ?? 0) < 18 },
  age: true,
};
const transformer = makeConditionalSchemaTransformer({ age: 17 })(schema, config);
transformer.run(); // throws: parentContactNumber is required
```

- `transformer.schema` — the transformed Zod schema
- `transformer.run()` — `transformer.schema.parse(data)`
- `transformer.staticConfig` — the config with conditionals removed, for `transformSchema`

Traversal, from `packages/core/src/index.ts`:

1. An optional field is unwrapped with `.unwrap()`.
2. Nested objects recurse with the nested config.
3. An array `'*'` config is applied to the element schema.
4. The new shape is copied back with object spread into `z.object`.

Fields absent from the config are kept.


# Streaming

Source: docs/streaming.md

---
title: "Streaming"
description: "Check a tool call while the JSON is still arriving."
answer: "@adaptate/core/stream checks a partial JSON document against each named config while text is still arriving. createAgUiPartialValidator turns AG-UI deltas into a partial value and a per-config result."
faq:
  - question: "What happens when a chunk cuts a string in half?"
    answer: "parsePartialJson closes the open string, objects, and arrays, so {\"title\":\"Pas becomes { title: \"Pas\" }."
  - question: "Does partial checking reject missing fields?"
    answer: "No. partial(value) keeps absent fields optional and still type-checks the fields that are present."
  - question: "Which peer does it need?"
    answer: "Only zod, version ^3.25.0 or ^4.0.0."
---

# Streaming

`@adaptate/core/stream` checks a partial document against each named config while text is still arriving. `zod` is the only peer.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Chunk["chunk"] --> PartialJson["parsePartialJson"]
  PartialJson --> Partial["partial(value)"]
  Value["complete value"] --> Final["final(value)"]
  Final --> Report["valid and errors per config"]
```

`parsePartialJson(text)` closes open strings, objects, and arrays, then parses the longest prefix. It returns `undefined` when nothing parses.

`createStreamValidator(schema, configs)`:

| Method | What it checks | Cache |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `partial(value)` | Present fields only. Absent fields stay optional. Every named config gets the same check. | Lenient schema on a `WeakMap` of the base schema, filled on first call. |
| `final(value)` | `transformSchema(schema, config).safeParse(value)` per name, returns `{ valid, errors }`. Takes a value, not text. | Transformed schemas built at creation. Later config edits do not change them. A config that cannot be transformed fails inside `final`. |

`validateStructuredOutput({ partial, final }, schema, configs)` runs those methods when the field is not `null`.

`createAgUiPartialValidator(schema, configs)` returns a push function:

| Event | Buffer key | Action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `TOOL_CALL_ARGS` | `toolCallId` | Append `delta`, parse, then `partial`. |
| `TEXT_MESSAGE_CONTENT` | `messageId` | Same. |
| `TOOL_CALL_END`, `TEXT_MESSAGE_END`, or `push.close(id)` | that id | Drop the buffer. |

A chunk that does not parse returns `undefined`. The same name on `@adaptate/core/stream-incremental` tokenizes each chunk once through `createPartialJsonFeed`.

```ts
import { z } from "zod";
import { createAgUiPartialValidator } from "@adaptate/core/stream";

const recipe = z.object({
  title: z.string().optional(),
  servings: z.number().optional(),
});
const push = createAgUiPartialValidator(recipe, {
  card: { title: true },
});
push({
  type: "TOOL_CALL_ARGS",
  toolCallId: "call-1",
  delta: '{"title":"Pas',
});
```

Streams partial JSON without re-reading what it already saw. Numbers: [Performance](performance.md#measured).

In v3, pass `makeFeed` to `fromAsyncIterableSteps` or `parseStream`. Runnable example: [v3 feeds](v3.md).


# v3 feeds

Source: docs/v3.md

---
title: "v3 feeds"
description: "A makeFeed hook on stream steps, so you can swap in a custom feed without rewriting the parser."
answer: "v3 adds a makeFeed hook to fromAsyncIterableSteps and parseStream. You keep openPath and tailOpen, and you can plug in the same kind of tracked feed already used by the default parser. The default feed is unchanged when you omit makeFeed."
faq:
  - question: "Do I have to write a feed?"
    answer: "No. The default feed is unchanged. Pass makeFeed only when you need a different source or a hooked verifier."
  - question: "Does this change existing imports?"
    answer: "No. fromAsyncIterableSteps and parseStream stay on their current subpaths. makeFeed is an optional argument."
---

# v3 feeds

A wrapping `makeFeed` around `createTrackedFeed`, passed to `parseStream` with a Zod schema and three JSON chunks.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Chunks["chunk iterable"] --> Parse["parseStream"]
  Schema["Zod schema"] --> Parse
  Feed["makeFeed"] --> Parse
  Parse --> Steps["steps with openPath and tailOpen"]
```

<!-- snippet: usages/make-feed.ts -->
```ts
import { parseStream } from "@adaptate/core/result";
import {
  createTrackedFeed,
  type TrackedFeed,
} from "@adaptate/core/stream-incremental";
import { z } from "zod";

export let recipe = z.object({
  title: z.string(),
  tags: z.array(z.string()),
});

export async function* chunks() {
  yield '{"title":"Pas';
  yield 'ta","tags":["c1","c';
  yield '2"]}';
}

export function makeFeed(): TrackedFeed {
  let inner = createTrackedFeed();
  return {
    push: (chunk) => inner.push(chunk),
    complete: () => inner.complete(),
    ended: () => inner.ended(),
    openPath: () => inner.openPath(),
    tailOpen: () => inner.tailOpen(),
  };
}

export async function collectRecipeSteps() {
  let steps = [];
  for await (let step of parseStream(
    chunks(),
    recipe,
    recipe.partial(),
    makeFeed,
  )) {
    steps.push({
      done: step.done,
      openPath: step.openPath,
      tailOpen: step.tailOpen,
      ok: step.result.ok,
      value: step.result.ok
        ? step.result.value
        : step.result.error,
    });
  }
  return steps;
}
```
<!-- /snippet -->

That stream yields:

| Step | done | openPath | tailOpen | result.value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | false | `["title"]` | true | `{ title: "Pas" }` |
| 2 | false | `["tags", 1]` | true | `{ title: "Pasta", tags: ["c1", "c"] }` |
| 3 | false | `[]` | false | `{ title: "Pasta", tags: ["c1", "c2"] }` |
| 4 | true | `[]` | false | `{ title: "Pasta", tags: ["c1", "c2"] }` |

Steps 1–3 are incremental. Step 4 is the final schema check.

| Need | Hook |
| --- | --- |
| Same stream, a different feed | Pass `makeFeed`. `openPath` and `tailOpen` stay on the step. |
| Verify bytes before they settle | Wrap the feed, or run `verifyBuffer` / `verifyStream`. See [Runtime verification](verification.md). |
| Large buffers | Optional `@adaptate/accel`. See [Acceleration](accel.md). |

`fromAsyncIterableSteps` takes the same `makeFeed` and yields `{ value, complete, openPath, tailOpen }`. [Streaming](streaming.md) covers the path already on npm. The [live benchmark](accel.md#live-benchmark) shows when WASM is worth adding.


# AG-UI

Source: docs/ag-ui.md

---
title: "AG-UI"
description: "Check AG-UI TOOL_CALL_ARGS deltas against each view while the JSON is still arriving."
answer: "createAgUiPartialValidator(schema, configs) returns a push function. Pass it each AG-UI TOOL_CALL_ARGS or TEXT_MESSAGE_CONTENT event, and it returns the partial value plus a valid flag for every named config."
faq:
  - question: "Which AG-UI events does push read?"
    answer: "TOOL_CALL_ARGS keyed by toolCallId and TEXT_MESSAGE_CONTENT keyed by messageId. TOOL_CALL_END and TEXT_MESSAGE_END drop the buffer for that id."
  - question: "Should I import it from /stream or /stream-incremental?"
    answer: "Both export createAgUiPartialValidator with the same shape. /stream-incremental tokenizes each chunk once, which matters for long tool calls."
  - question: "What does push return for a chunk that does not parse yet?"
    answer: "undefined. The next chunk that completes a value returns a result."
---

# AG-UI

An AG-UI agent streams a tool call as `TOOL_CALL_ARGS` events. Each event carries a `delta` of JSON text. `push` keeps one buffer per `toolCallId` and checks the partial value against every named config.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Agent["AG-UI agent"] -->|"TOOL_CALL_ARGS delta"| Push["push(event)"]
  Push --> Buffer["buffer per toolCallId"]
  Buffer --> Partial["partial value"]
  Partial --> Card["card config"]
  Partial --> Kitchen["kitchen config"]
```

```ts
import { z } from "zod";
import { createAgUiPartialValidator } from "@adaptate/core/stream-incremental";

const push = createAgUiPartialValidator(
  z.object({ title: z.string(), servings: z.number() }),
  { card: { title: true } },
);
const check = push({ type: "TOOL_CALL_ARGS", toolCallId: "call-1", delta: '{"title":"Pas' });
```

`check.partial` is `{ title: "Pas" }` and `check.results.card.valid` is `true`. `JSON.parse` on the same text throws.

The file below is typechecked and run by the site tests. It builds the re-parse and incremental validators for one order schema.

<!-- snippet: usages/ag-ui.ts -->
```ts
import { createAgUiPartialValidator as createReparseAgUi } from "@adaptate/core/stream";
import { createAgUiPartialValidator as createIncrementalAgUi } from "@adaptate/core/stream-incremental";

import { cardConfig, orderSchema } from "../order-schema";

export function createReparseOrderValidator() {
  return createReparseAgUi(orderSchema, { card: cardConfig });
}

export function createIncrementalOrderValidator() {
  return createIncrementalAgUi(orderSchema, { card: cardConfig });
}
```
<!-- /snippet -->

The order schema and the card config:

<!-- snippet: order-schema.ts -->
```ts
import type { Config } from "@adaptate/core";
import { z } from "zod";

export let orderSchema = z.object({
  title: z.string(),
  notes: z.string(),
  items: z.array(
    z.object({
      sku: z.string(),
      qty: z.number(),
    }),
  ),
});

export let partialOrderSchema = orderSchema.partial();

export let cardConfig = {
  title: true,
} satisfies Config<z.infer<typeof partialOrderSchema>>;
```
<!-- /snippet -->

See [Streaming](streaming.md) for `partial` and `final`.


# Web streams

Source: docs/web-streams.md

---
title: "Web streams"
description: "Feed a ReadableStream, server-sent events, or a Node stream into the incremental parser."
answer: "fromAsyncIterable from @adaptate/core/stream-incremental reads any async sequence of strings or UTF-8 bytes and yields a partial value after each chunk. A ReadableStream, an SSE response, and a Node Readable all become that sequence."
faq:
  - question: "Do I need an SDK to read OpenAI or Anthropic deltas?"
    answer: "No. A small async generator maps each provider event to its argument text, and fromAsyncIterable reads that."
  - question: "Can I read server-sent events from fetch?"
    answer: "Yes. Read response.body, split blocks on a blank line, and pass each data line to your handler."
  - question: "Does it work in Node pipelines?"
    answer: "Yes. Pass the pipeline source to fromAsyncIterable inside stream/promises pipeline."
---

# Web streams

Every source below ends in the same place: an async sequence of strings or bytes that `fromAsyncIterable` turns into partial values.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Web["ReadableStream"] --> Iter["async iterable of strings or bytes"]
  Sse["SSE response or EventSource"] --> Iter
  Node["Node Readable"] --> Iter
  Iter --> Feed["fromAsyncIterable"]
  Feed --> Value["partial value per chunk"]
```

```ts
import { fromAsyncIterable } from "@adaptate/core/stream-incremental";

async function* chunks() {
  yield '{"title":';
  yield '"Pas';
}

for await (const partialValue of fromAsyncIterable(chunks())) {
  console.log(partialValue);
}
```

## ReadableStream

<!-- snippet: usages/web-readable.ts -->
```ts
import { fromAsyncIterable } from "@adaptate/core/stream-incremental";

export async function* iterateReadable(
  stream: ReadableStream<Uint8Array>,
): AsyncGenerator<Uint8Array> {
  let reader = stream.getReader();
  try {
    for (;;) {
      let step = await reader.read();
      if (step.done) return;
      if (step.value) yield step.value;
    }
  } finally {
    reader.releaseLock();
  }
}

export async function collectWebStream(stream: ReadableStream<Uint8Array>): Promise<unknown[]> {
  let partials: unknown[] = [];
  for await (let partialValue of fromAsyncIterable(iterateReadable(stream))) {
    partials.push(partialValue);
  }
  return partials;
}
```
<!-- /snippet -->

## Server-sent events

<!-- snippet: usages/sse.ts -->
```ts
export function frameSseData(delta: string): string {
  return `data: ${delta}\n\n`;
}

export async function readSse(response: Response, onDelta: (delta: string) => void): Promise<void> {
  let body = response.body;
  if (!body) return;
  let reader = body.getReader();
  let decoder = new TextDecoder();
  let buffer = "";
  try {
    for (;;) {
      let step = await reader.read();
      if (step.done) {
        buffer += decoder.decode();
        break;
      }
      buffer += decoder.decode(step.value, { stream: true });
      buffer = emitSseBlocks(buffer, onDelta);
    }
    emitSseBlocks(`${buffer}\n\n`, onDelta);
  } finally {
    reader.releaseLock();
  }
}

export function attachEventSource(source: EventSource, onDelta: (delta: string) => void): () => void {
  let onMessage = (event: MessageEvent) => {
    if (typeof event.data !== "string") return;
    if (event.data.length === 0 || event.data === "[DONE]") return;
    onDelta(event.data);
  };
  source.addEventListener("message", onMessage);
  return () => {
    source.removeEventListener("message", onMessage);
  };
}

export async function readSseFromFetch(
  input: RequestInfo | URL,
  onDelta: (delta: string) => void,
): Promise<void> {
  let response = await fetch(input);
  await readSse(response, onDelta);
}

function emitSseBlocks(buffer: string, onDelta: (delta: string) => void): string {
  let separator = buffer.indexOf("\n\n");
  while (separator >= 0) {
    let block = buffer.slice(0, separator);
    buffer = buffer.slice(separator + 2);
    emitSseBlock(block, onDelta);
    separator = buffer.indexOf("\n\n");
  }
  return buffer;
}

function emitSseBlock(block: string, onDelta: (delta: string) => void): void {
  let dataLines: string[] = [];
  for (let line of block.split("\n")) {
    if (!line.startsWith("data:")) continue;
    let value = line.slice("data:".length);
    dataLines.push(value.startsWith(" ") ? value.slice(1) : value);
  }
  if (dataLines.length === 0) return;
  let data = dataLines.join("\n");
  if (data.length === 0 || data === "[DONE]") return;
  onDelta(data);
}
```
<!-- /snippet -->

## Node streams and provider deltas

<!-- snippet: usages/node-stream.ts -->
```ts
import { Readable } from "node:stream";
import { pipeline } from "node:stream/promises";
import { fromAsyncIterable } from "@adaptate/core/stream-incremental";

export type OpenAiToolChunk = {
  choices?: Array<{
    delta?: {
      tool_calls?: Array<{
        function?: {
          arguments?: string;
        };
      }>;
    };
  }>;
};

export type AnthropicInputChunk = {
  delta?: {
    type?: string;
    partial_json?: string;
  };
};

export async function* openAiArguments(
  events: AsyncIterable<OpenAiToolChunk>,
): AsyncGenerator<string> {
  for await (let event of events) {
    let delta = event.choices?.[0]?.delta?.tool_calls?.[0]?.function?.arguments;
    if (typeof delta === "string" && delta.length > 0) yield delta;
  }
}

export async function* anthropicInputJson(
  events: AsyncIterable<AnthropicInputChunk>,
): AsyncGenerator<string> {
  for await (let event of events) {
    let delta = event.delta;
    if (
      delta?.type === "input_json_delta" &&
      typeof delta.partial_json === "string" &&
      delta.partial_json.length > 0
    ) {
      yield delta.partial_json;
    }
  }
}

export async function collectNodeStream(readable: Readable): Promise<unknown[]> {
  let partials: unknown[] = [];
  await pipeline(readable, async function collect(source) {
    for await (let partialValue of fromAsyncIterable(source as AsyncIterable<string | Uint8Array>)) {
      partials.push(partialValue);
    }
  });
  return partials;
}
```
<!-- /snippet -->

Each file is typechecked and run by the site tests.


# OpenAPI

Source: docs/openapi.md

---
title: "OpenAPI"
description: "Turn an OpenAPI schema into Zod, and write a Zod schema back out."
answer: "@adaptate/utils converts an OpenAPI schema to Zod with openAPISchemaToZod, writes a Zod schema back out with zodToOpenAPISchema, and loads a spec from disk or the web with full $ref resolution."
faq:
  - question: "Can I load a YAML spec?"
    answer: "Yes, with getDereferencedOpenAPIDocument. Install the optional peer js-yaml to parse YAML."
  - question: "Can a converted schema have views?"
    answer: "Yes. openAPISchemaToZod returns a Zod object, and transformSchema adds the per-view required fields."
  - question: "Which OpenAPI keywords are supported?"
    answer: "Types, enums, string formats and lengths, number bounds, array bounds, allOf, anyOf, oneOf, nullable, required, and resolved $ref."
---

# OpenAPI

`@adaptate/utils` converts OpenAPI schemas and Zod schemas, and loads a spec. Peer: `zod@^3.25.0 || ^4.0.0`. See [Optional peers](optional-peers.md) for YAML and remote `$ref`s.

```ts
import { getDereferencedOpenAPIDocument, openAPISchemaToZod, zodToOpenAPISchema } from "@adaptate/utils";
import { z } from "zod";

const doc = await getDereferencedOpenAPIDocument({
  location: "filesystem",
  callSiteURL: import.meta.url,
  relativePathToSpecFile: "./api-spec.yml",
});

const fromWeb = await getDereferencedOpenAPIDocument({
  location: "web",
  webURL: "https://api.apis.guru/v2/specs/googleapis.com/books/v1/openapi.yaml",
});

const zodSchema = openAPISchemaToZod({
  type: "object",
  required: ["age"],
  properties: {
    name: { type: "string", minLength: 2 },
    age: { type: "integer", minimum: 0 },
    email: { type: "string", format: "email" },
    tags: { type: "array", items: { type: "string" }, minItems: 1 },
  },
});
zodSchema.parse({ name: "Ada", age: 25, email: "ada@example.com", tags: ["dev"] });

const openAPISchema = zodToOpenAPISchema(
  z.object({
    name: z.string().min(2).describe("Full name"),
    age: z.number().int().min(0),
    email: z.email().optional(),
    tags: z.array(z.string()).min(1),
  }),
);
```

`openAPISchemaToZod` supports `string`, `number`, `integer`, `boolean`, `object`, `array`, `enum`, `minLength`, `maxLength`, `pattern`, string `format` (email, uuid, url, date-time, date), `minimum` / `maximum`, `exclusiveMinimum` / `exclusiveMaximum`, `multipleOf`, `minItems` / `maxItems`, `allOf` (`.and()`), `anyOf` / `oneOf` (`.union()`), `nullable`, object `required`, and a `$ref` that is already resolved.

`zodToOpenAPISchema` writes `required` without `.optional()` fields, `.nullable()`, string min/max/regex/formats, number min/max (inclusive and exclusive), `multipleOf`, integer, array `minItems` / `maxItems`, `z.enum` (string enums and numeric member tuples; Zod 4 folded `z.nativeEnum` into `z.enum`), `z.union` as `anyOf`, `.describe()`, `ZodDate`, and `ZodBigInt`.

`json-schema-to-zod` and `zod-to-json-schema` cover cases these two functions do not.

## Views from an OpenAPI schema

The file below is typechecked and run by the site tests. It converts an OpenAPI object to Zod, then requires the title for a card view.

<!-- snippet: usages/openapi.ts -->
```ts
import { transformSchema } from "@adaptate/core";
import { openAPISchemaToZod } from "@adaptate/utils/openapi";
import { z } from "zod";

export let orderOpenApiSchema = {
  type: "object",
  required: ["title"],
  properties: {
    title: { type: "string" },
    notes: { type: "string" },
    items: {
      type: "array",
      items: {
        type: "object",
        required: ["sku", "qty"],
        properties: {
          sku: { type: "string" },
          qty: { type: "integer" },
        },
      },
    },
  },
};

let cardSchema: z.ZodType | undefined;

export function cardSchemaFromOpenApi(): z.ZodType {
  if (cardSchema) return cardSchema;
  let converted = openAPISchemaToZod(orderOpenApiSchema);
  if (!(converted instanceof z.ZodObject)) {
    throw new Error("OpenAPI order schema was not an object");
  }
  cardSchema = transformSchema(converted, { title: true });
  return cardSchema;
}

export function openApiCardReady(order: { title?: string }): boolean {
  return cardSchemaFromOpenApi().safeParse(order).success;
}
```
<!-- /snippet -->


# Zod

Source: docs/zod.md

---
title: "Zod"
description: "Use one Zod schema with a Config per view, and check it through the Standard Schema interface."
answer: "Write one Zod schema, then give each view a Config that marks the fields it needs. transformSchema(schema.partial(), config) returns a Zod schema for that view, and validateStandard checks it through ~standard."
faq:
  - question: "Which Zod versions are supported?"
    answer: "zod ^3.25.0 or ^4.0.0, as a peer dependency."
  - question: "Is the result still a Zod schema?"
    answer: "Yes. It has parse, safeParse, and the ~standard interface, so any Standard Schema consumer can use it."
  - question: "How does Config catch mistakes?"
    answer: "Config<T> only accepts field paths that exist on T, so a typo fails at compile time."
---

# Zod

One schema describes the data. Each view states which fields it needs. A title alone passes the card and fails the kitchen.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Schema["recipe schema"] --> Partial["schema.partial()"]
  Partial -->|"card config"| Card["card schema"]
  Partial -->|"kitchen config"| Kitchen["kitchen schema"]
  Card --> Standard["~standard validate"]
```

```ts
import { z } from "zod";
import { transformSchema } from "@adaptate/core";

const recipe = z.object({ title: z.string(), servings: z.number() });
transformSchema(recipe.partial(), { title: true }).parse({ title: "Pas" });
```

The file below is typechecked and run by the site tests.

<!-- snippet: usages/zod.ts -->
```ts
import { transformSchema, type Config } from "@adaptate/core";
import { validateStandard } from "@adaptate/core/standard";
import { z } from "zod";

export let recipeSchema = z.object({
  title: z.string(),
  servings: z.number(),
});

export type Recipe = z.infer<typeof recipeSchema>;

export let cardConfig = { title: true } satisfies Config<Recipe>;
export let kitchenConfig = { title: true, servings: true } satisfies Config<Recipe>;

export let cardSchema = transformSchema(recipeSchema.partial(), cardConfig);
export let kitchenSchema = transformSchema(recipeSchema.partial(), kitchenConfig);

export function readyViews(recipe: Partial<Recipe>) {
  return {
    card: cardSchema.safeParse(recipe).success,
    kitchen: kitchenSchema.safeParse(recipe).success,
  };
}

export async function checkWithStandardSchema(recipe: unknown) {
  return validateStandard(cardSchema, recipe);
}
```
<!-- /snippet -->

`validateStandard` comes from `@adaptate/core/standard`. It accepts any schema with `~standard.validate`, so a valibot or ArkType schema works the same way. See [Transform](transform.md) for config values and [TypeScript](typescript.md) for the published types.


# Effect

Source: docs/effect.md

---
title: "Effect"
description: "Run the same checks in an Effect pipeline. Effect is an optional peer."
answer: "@adaptate/core/effect runs the same adaptate checks inside an Effect pipeline. createEffectStreamValidator returns effects that fail with AdaptateParseError or AdaptateValidationError. effect is an optional peer."
faq:
  - question: "Does importing @adaptate/core load effect?"
    answer: "No. Only @adaptate/core/effect imports effect."
  - question: "Does an unmet config fail final(text)?"
    answer: "No. final(text) reports { valid, issues } per config. final(text, configName) fails when that config is not met."
---

# Effect

`@adaptate/core/effect` needs the optional peer `effect@^4.0.0`. Importing `@adaptate/core` or `@adaptate/core/stream` does not load `effect`. Validation is not retried.

```ts
import { Effect } from "effect";
import { z } from "zod";
import { createEffectStreamValidator } from "@adaptate/core/effect";

const recipe = z.object({
  title: z.string().optional(),
  servings: z.number().optional(),
});
const validator = createEffectStreamValidator(recipe, {
  card: { title: true },
  kitchen: { servings: true },
});

const report = Effect.runSync(validator.final('{"title":"Pasta"}'));
// report.value is { title: "Pasta" }
// report.configs.card is { valid: true, issues: null }
// report.configs.kitchen.valid is false

const card = Effect.runSync(validator.final('{"title":"Pasta"}', "card"));
// { title: "Pasta" }
```

`createEffectStreamValidator` builds the per-config `transformSchema` results when the validator is created, and `final(text)` reuses them. The lenient partial schema is cached on the base schema at the first partial check. A schema that cannot be transformed, such as `z.string()`, still fails inside `final` with `configName: "schema"`. Config objects are read at creation. `final(text, configName)` calls `transformSchema` for that config.

`final(text)` parses with `JSON.parse`. Bad or truncated text fails with `AdaptateParseError`. The base schema is then parsed; that failure is `AdaptateValidationError` with `configName: "schema"`. On success the effect succeeds with `{ value, configs }`. Each named config is `{ valid, issues }`. An unmet config does not fail the effect. A mutated config is read by value on the next `final`.

`final(text, configName)` parses, then validates with `transformSchema(schema, configs[configName])`. Failure is `AdaptateValidationError` with that `configName`. Success is the parsed value. `configName` is typed as `keyof` the configs object. If the runtime name is not an own key of `configs`, the effect fails with `AdaptateValidationError` and one custom issue, `unknown config`, instead of validating the base schema. A mutated config is read on this path, because this path calls `transformSchema` again.

`validate(schema, config, value)` is `transformSchema(schema, config).parse`, failing as `AdaptateValidationError` with `configName: "config"`.

`validatePartial(schema, configs, partial)` fails on the first config that has errors, keeping that config's Zod issues. A thrown `ZodError` is kept as issues. Any other thrown cause becomes one custom issue with the error message.

`partial(value)` is the lenient stream report. `agUi(event)` and `agUiStream(events)` wrap `createAgUiPartialValidator` from `@adaptate/core/stream`. That path appends to a buffer and calls `parsePartialJson`. It does not load `@adaptate/core/stream-incremental`. Pass a third argument, `makeFeed`, and those two methods call that feed instead. Omit it and they keep the re-parse feed.

## A typechecked example

The site tests run this file with `Effect.runPromise`. A missing title falls back on `AdaptateValidationError`. Truncated JSON still fails with `AdaptateParseError`.

<!-- snippet: usages/effect.ts -->
```ts
import { Effect } from "effect";
import { createEffectStreamValidator } from "@adaptate/core/effect";
import { z } from "zod";

let recipe = z.object({
  title: z.string().optional(),
  servings: z.number().optional(),
});

export let recipeValidator = createEffectStreamValidator(recipe, {
  card: { title: true },
  kitchen: { servings: true },
});

export function finalReport(text: string) {
  return Effect.runPromise(recipeValidator.final(text));
}

export function cardOrFallback(text: string) {
  return Effect.runPromise(
    recipeValidator.final(text, "card").pipe(
      Effect.catchTag("AdaptateValidationError", () => Effect.succeed({ title: "Untitled" })),
    ),
  );
}
```
<!-- /snippet -->


# Find your choke points

Source: docs/choke-points.md

---
title: "Find your choke points"
description: "Guard the few places where bad or partial data breaks an app, with a Result that keeps an ok track and an error track."
answer: "A choke point is a boundary where untrusted data enters: an API or SI model response, a stream, a form, an import, a config file. parse from @adaptate/core/result returns ok or err, so map, flatMap, and recover keep each track explicit. parseStream does the same for streamed JSON."
faq:
  - question: "Which schemas does parse accept?"
    answer: "Any Standard Schema: Zod, Valibot, ArkType, or a schema from openAPISchemaToZod in @adaptate/utils. Use parseAsync for schemas that validate asynchronously."
  - question: "What is on the error track?"
    answer: "The Standard Schema issues, each with a message and a path. mapError turns them into your own error type."
  - question: "How does parseStream fit the incremental parser?"
    answer: "It reads chunks through fromAsyncIterableSteps from @adaptate/core/stream-incremental and checks each partial value against an optional partial schema. The last step checks the closed value against the full schema, or errs when the stream ends without one complete JSON value."
---

# Find your choke points

Most of an app trusts data that one small boundary already checked. Find those boundaries and give each one two tracks.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Input["untrusted input or stream"] --> Parse["parse or parseStream"]
  Parse -->|"ok"| Value["typed value"]
  Parse -->|"err"| Issues["issues"]
  Value -->|"map, flatMap"| Next["next step"]
  Issues -->|"recover, mapError"| Report["fallback or report"]
```

| Choke point | Schema source | Call |
| --- | --- | --- |
| API response | OpenAPI via `openAPISchemaToZod` | `parse` |
| SI tool call | Zod | `parseStream` |
| Form or import | Zod or JSON Schema | `parse` |
| Async refinement | any Standard Schema | `parseAsync` |

```ts
import { parse } from "@adaptate/core/result";

parse(schema, input).map(render).recover(showIssues);
```

The file below is typechecked and run by the site tests.

<!-- snippet: usages/choke-points.ts -->
```ts
import { parse, parseStream, type Issues } from "@adaptate/core/result";
import { openAPISchemaToZod } from "@adaptate/utils";
import { z } from "zod";

export let invoiceSchema = openAPISchemaToZod({
  type: "object",
  required: ["id", "total"],
  properties: {
    id: { type: "string", minLength: 1 },
    total: { type: "number", minimum: 0 },
  },
});

function fields(issues: Issues): string {
  return issues
    .map((issue) => {
      let first = issue.path?.[0];
      return String(typeof first === "object" ? first.key : (first ?? "input"));
    })
    .join(", ");
}

export function checkInvoice(input: unknown): string {
  return parse(invoiceSchema, input).match(
    () => "accepted",
    (issues) => `check ${fields(issues)}`,
  );
}

let toolArguments = z.object({ city: z.string(), days: z.number().int().positive() });

type Trip = { city: string; days: number; nights: number };
export type ToolCallOutcome = { previews: string[]; call?: Trip; issues?: string[] };

export async function readToolCall(chunks: AsyncIterable<string>): Promise<ToolCallOutcome> {
  let previews: string[] = [];
  let outcome: ToolCallOutcome = { previews };
  for await (let step of parseStream(chunks, toolArguments, toolArguments.partial())) {
    if (!step.done) {
      if (step.result.ok && step.result.value.city) previews.push(step.result.value.city);
      continue;
    }
    outcome = step.result
      .map((call) => ({ ...call, nights: call.days - 1 }))
      .match<ToolCallOutcome>(
        (call) => ({ previews, call }),
        (issues) => ({ previews, issues: issues.map((issue) => issue.message) }),
      );
  }
  return outcome;
}
```
<!-- /snippet -->

Each `parseStream` step also carries `openPath` and `tailOpen`. A partial step checks the fields that are present; a field off `openPath` is final unless the document repeats a key on that path later (`JSON.parse` lets the last duplicate win). `tailOpen` is true while the last value on `openPath` is a cut-off string, number or keyword, so `"c"` in `{"comments":["c1","c` may still become `"c2"`. `isSettled(step, path)` tells you whether one path is final: `true` for any present path once the step is complete, `false` for a path that has not arrived, and `false` on a partial step whose partial schema failed (it has no `result.value`). A string with a raw control character or a bad escape stays open, and so does a number or keyword glued to a character other than whitespace, `,`, `}` or `]` (`12-3`, `truex`). Neither is ever settled. Both fields are non-enumerable, so `toEqual` and JSON of a step do not change.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Root["root"] --> Comments["comments"] --> C1["0: c1 (final)"]
  Comments --> C["1: c (tailOpen)"]
```

`parseStream` reads strict JSON only, with no revivers or references. That kind of revival is how CVE-2025-55182 (React Server Components, CVSS 10.0, December 2025) became remote code execution.


# TypeScript

Source: docs/typescript.md

---
title: "TypeScript"
description: "Types ship in the npm package. CI checks them on TypeScript 7 and 6."
answer: "The adaptate packages ship their .d.ts files. Value types are inferred from the Zod schema, and CI typechecks the packed tarballs on TypeScript 7 and 6 with bundler, node16, and nodenext resolution."
faq:
  - question: "Do I need @types packages?"
    answer: "No. Types ship inside @adaptate/core and @adaptate/utils."
  - question: "Is Config type-checked?"
    answer: "Yes. Config<T> checks field paths at compile time, including '*' on arrays."
---

# TypeScript

The published packages include their `.d.ts` files. A value's type is inferred from the Zod schema you pass in.

```ts
import { z } from "zod";
import { transformSchema, type Config } from "@adaptate/core";

const recipe = z.object({ title: z.string(), servings: z.number() });
type Recipe = z.infer<typeof recipe>;
const card = { title: true } satisfies Config<Recipe>;
const cardSchema = transformSchema(recipe.partial(), card);
```

`scripts/ts-consumer-check.mjs` packs `@adaptate/core` and `@adaptate/utils`, installs the tarballs, and typechecks a consumer that imports every published entry.

The CI job `ts7-consumer` runs that script on TypeScript 7 and TypeScript 6, each with `moduleResolution` `bundler`, `node16`, and `nodenext`.


# Subpaths

Source: docs/subpaths.md

---
title: "Subpaths"
description: "The published entry points, and which peers each one loads."
answer: "@adaptate/core publishes seven entry points: the root, /stream, /stream-incremental, /standard, /effect, /result, and /verify. zod is the only required peer, and effect loads only from /effect. Optional acceleration lives in separate packages, not in core."
faq:
  - question: "Which entry point should a chat UI use?"
    answer: "@adaptate/core/stream-incremental for long streams, or @adaptate/core/stream for the re-parse path and createFrameThrottle."
  - question: "Which @adaptate/utils path loads a spec from disk?"
    answer: "@adaptate/utils/openapi or @adaptate/utils/ssr."
---

# Subpaths

`@adaptate/core` publishes seven entries and has no `dependencies`. `zod@^3.25.0 || ^4.0.0` is the required peer. `effect@^4.0.0` is an optional peer and is imported only by `@adaptate/core/effect`.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  zod["zod peer"] --> core["@adaptate/core"]
  zod --> stream["@adaptate/core/stream"]
  zod --> incremental["@adaptate/core/stream-incremental"]
  zod --> standard["@adaptate/core/standard"]
  zod --> effect["@adaptate/core/effect"]
  zod --> result["@adaptate/core/result"]
  zod --> verify["@adaptate/core/verify"]
  effectPeer["effect optional peer"] -.-> effect
```

| Entry | Exports |
| --- | --- |
| `@adaptate/core` | `transformSchema`, `makeConditionalSchemaTransformer`, `transformPartialSchema`, `validatePartialAgainstConfigs`, `makeStreamingConditionalTransformer`, `Config`, `DeepPartial`, `PartialValidationResult` |
| `@adaptate/core/stream` | `parsePartialJson`, `createStreamValidator`, `validateStructuredOutput`, `createAgUiPartialValidator`, `agUiValidatorWith`, `reparseFeed`, `createFrameThrottle`, `AgUiDeltaEvent`, `PartialJsonFeed` |
| `@adaptate/core/stream-incremental` | `createPartialJsonFeed`, `fromAsyncIterable`, `fromAsyncIterableSteps`, `isSettled`, `createAgUiPartialValidator`, `PartialJsonFeed`, `JsonStreamStep`, `TrackedStep`, `JsonPath` |
| `@adaptate/core/standard` | `isStandardSchema`, `validateStandard`, `validateAgainstStandardSchemas`, `StandardSchemaV1`, `StandardIssue`, `StandardResult`, `StandardValidationResult` |
| `@adaptate/core/result` | `parse`, `parseAsync`, `parseStream`, `ok`, `err`, `isResult`, `isSettled`, `Result`, `Ok`, `Err`, `Track`, `Issues`, `StreamStep`, `JsonPath` |
| `@adaptate/core/effect` | `validate`, `validatePartial`, `createEffectStreamValidator`, `AdaptateValidationError`, `AdaptateParseError`, `ConfigReport`, `FinalReport` |
| `@adaptate/core/verify` | `hashBuffer`, `hexFromBytes`, `normalizeHex`, `verifiersFrom`, `verifyBuffer`, `verifyStream`, `Verifier`, `VerifyContext`, `VerifyFailure`, `VerifyManifest`, `HashAlgorithm`, `VerifyCheck`, `VerifyResult` |

`@adaptate/core/stream-incremental` also exports `createTrackedFeed` and `TrackedFeed`, which `makeFeed` returns.

Optional Advanced packages are not core subpaths and are not pulled in by `@adaptate/core`:

| Package | What it is for |
| --- | --- |
| `@adaptate/accel` | Probe and size-route large-buffer or batched in-memory work |
| `@adaptate/wasm` | Portable C ABI WASM. Browsers should import `@adaptate/wasm/runtime` so `node:fs` does not enter the bundle. |
| `@adaptate/native` | Node-API bindings, including an optional hardware GPU path above 4 MiB |

`@adaptate/utils` has no required runtime dependencies. Its peers are in [Optional peers](optional-peers.md). Published paths:

| Import | Runtime file |
| --- | --- |
| `@adaptate/utils` | `build/index.es.js` (browser bundle; Node builtins are external) |
| `@adaptate/utils/openapi` | `ssr-build/openapi.js` |
| `@adaptate/utils/ssr` | `ssr-build/index.js` |

Use `/ssr` or `/openapi` when loading a spec from disk.


# Optional peers

Source: docs/optional-peers.md

---
title: "Optional peers"
description: "effect, js-yaml, and the ref parser load only when that code is imported. Acceleration packages are separate optional installs."
answer: "effect, js-yaml, and the JSON Schema ref parser are optional peers and load only when that code is imported. zod is the only required peer. @adaptate/accel, @adaptate/wasm, and @adaptate/native are separate optional packages, not core peers, and they leave the default install zero-dep."
faq:
  - question: "Do I need js-yaml for JSON specs?"
    answer: "No. js-yaml loads only while parsing YAML."
  - question: "When is the ref parser needed?"
    answer: "Only for remote or file $ref pointers. In-document $ref pointers use the local resolver."
---

# Optional peers

| Package | Peer | When it loads |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `@adaptate/core` | `effect@^4.0.0` | Only `@adaptate/core/effect` |
| `@adaptate/utils` | `js-yaml@^5.5.0` | Only while parsing YAML |
| `@adaptate/utils` | `@apidevtools/json-schema-ref-parser@^16.0.8` | Only for a remote or file `$ref` |

`zod@^3.25.0 || ^4.0.0` is required for both packages. Neither package has a `dependencies` field.

In-document `$ref` pointers use the local resolver (`packages/utils/src/dereference-local.ts`). JSON specs need no extra package.

A missing YAML parser throws:

```
Optional peer dependency "js-yaml" is required to parse YAML. Install it with `pnpm add js-yaml`.
```

A missing ref parser throws:

```
Optional peer dependency "@apidevtools/json-schema-ref-parser" is required to resolve remote or file $ref pointers. Install it with `pnpm add @apidevtools/json-schema-ref-parser`.
```

js-yaml 5 ships its own types. `@types/js-yaml` is not a dependency.


# Acceleration

Source: docs/accel.md

---
title: "Acceleration"
description: "Optional native, WASM, and GPU packages for large buffers, kept off the default zero-dep install."
answer: "Optional @adaptate/accel, @adaptate/wasm, and @adaptate/native packages help with large buffers or batched in-memory verification. adaptate and @adaptate/core stay zero-dependency. Skip them for small ~3 µs streaming chunks, where pure JS is already faster."
faq:
  - question: "Do I need to install accel to use adaptate?"
    answer: "No. adaptate and @adaptate/core work without it. Add an acceleration package only when buffers are large enough to benefit, or when you embed the Rust/WASM core in a host."
  - question: "When does acceleration actually help?"
    answer: "On large buffers, multi-MB in-memory verification, batched checks, or a Rust/WASM host embed. Measured SHA-256 at 1 KiB, 32 KiB, and 2 MiB was faster in JS than WASM or native. Small streaming chunks should stay on zero-dep JS."
  - question: "When does GPU run?"
    answer: "Only above a 4 MiB threshold, and only when a hardware GPU is present. A software renderer is ignored, and the work falls back to native, then WASM, then JavaScript."
---

# Acceleration

Skip this for ordinary JS objects, buffers under ~32 KiB, and ~3 µs streaming chunks. `@adaptate/core` stays zero-dependency. `@adaptate/accel`, `@adaptate/native`, and `@adaptate/wasm` are optional Advanced add-ons.

## When it makes sense

| Use it | Leave it out |
| --- | --- |
| Multi-MB in-memory [runtime verification](verification.md) (#84) | Small streaming chunks (~3 µs JS parser) |
| Batched hash or manifest checks | Buffers under ~32 KiB |
| A Rust or WASM host embed of the C ABI core | The default zero-dep install |

## Native, WASM, and GPU

`@adaptate/accel` probes the runtime and size-routes the work. JavaScript is the fallback at every step.

| Path | Package | When it is considered |
| --- | --- | --- |
| JavaScript | `@adaptate/core` / the JS fallback in `@adaptate/accel` | Default. JS objects, buffers under ~32 KiB, and any runtime that has no optional backend. |
| Native | `@adaptate/native` | Node-API (CPU SIMD, worker threads) for large buffers on Node. |
| WASM | `@adaptate/wasm` | A portable C ABI module (`wasm32-simd128`) for browsers or hosts that can instantiate `/adaptate_accel.wasm`. Import `@adaptate/wasm/runtime` in a browser so `node:fs` never enters the bundle. |
| GPU | `@adaptate/native` (`gpu` feature) | Only for hash or batch work at or above 4 MiB, and only when a hardware GPU is present. A software renderer is ignored. |

```ts
import { verifyInMemory } from "@adaptate/accel";

const checked = await verifyInMemory(bytes, {
  sha256: expectedDigest,
});
```

`verifyInMemory` probes `@adaptate/native` and `@adaptate/wasm` when they are installed, then falls back to JavaScript. A browser can ship `@adaptate/wasm` without the Node-API package. A Node service can use `@adaptate/native` and skip WASM.

## Measured numbers

Medians from a real-binary Track 2 run (SHA-256, 7 runs unless noted). JS is `@adaptate/core/verify` / Web Crypto. No number is mocked.

| Work | Size | JS median | Cached WASM median | Native median |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| SHA-256 | 1 KiB | 0.003 ms | 0.034 ms | 0.037 ms |
| SHA-256 | 32 KiB | 0.020 ms | 0.101 ms | 0.057 ms |
| SHA-256 | 2 MiB | 1.181 ms | 6.251 ms | 1.688 ms |
| verify | 1 KiB | 0.006 ms | 0.047 ms | 0.039 ms |
| verify | 32 KiB | 0.020 ms | 0.103 ms | 0.057 ms |
| verify | 2 MiB | 1.166 ms | 6.242 ms | 1.740 ms |

| Note | Result |
| --- | --- |
| WASM bindings, cold first hash | 6.394 ms |
| WASM bindings, later cached hash | 0.104 ms |
| Digests | Matched JS on every size above |
| 4 MiB GPU probe | Software renderer only, so GPU stayed unavailable. Native 3.274 ms (3 runs), JS 2.391 ms. Native batch of the same payload: 3.080 ms. |
| UTF-8 scan | `café — こんにちは` and `ä` buffers at 1 KiB, 32 KiB, and 2 MiB: JS, WASM, and native agreed. |

These tables are one host. The [live benchmark](#live-benchmark) on this page runs the same JS vs WASM hash in your browser, with a digest check.

Pair this with [`makeFeed`](v3.md) when the bytes arrive as a stream, and with [runtime verification](verification.md) when a buffer must be checked before anything is stored. Citations: [Proof](proof.md).


# Runtime verification

Source: docs/verification.md

---
title: "Runtime verification"
description: "Fail-closed in-memory hooks that verify a buffer before any bytes are written to disk."
answer: "v3 adds @adaptate/core/verify for fail-closed in-memory checks (issue 84). hashBuffer, verifyBuffer, and verifyStream can hash a buffer, check size, type, or name, and run a formal or custom verifier — all before anything is written. If a check fails, the bytes stay in memory and are discarded."
faq:
  - question: "What happens when a check fails?"
    answer: "The hook fails closed. Nothing is stored. You get a typed error for the check that failed, and the buffer is discarded."
  - question: "Can I add my own check?"
    answer: "Yes. Built-in hooks cover hash and metadata. Pass formal or custom verifiers for a spec or an extra property. Antivirus engines are out of scope."
---

# Runtime verification

A download or a stream should not touch the disk until it has been checked. [Issue 84](https://github.com/p10ns11y/adaptate/issues/84) is covered by `@adaptate/core/verify`.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Bytes["buffer"] --> VerifyBuf["verifyBuffer"]
  Chunks["chunks"] --> VerifyStream["verifyStream"]
  VerifyBuf -->|"ok"| Keep["checked bytes"]
  VerifyBuf -->|"fail"| Drop["discard, typed error"]
  VerifyStream -->|"ok"| Keep
  VerifyStream -->|"fail"| Drop
```

| Check | When it runs | On failure |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SHA-256 (or SHA-384 / SHA-512) | Over the in-memory bytes | Typed hash error, bytes discarded |
| Size, media type, name | Against an expected manifest | Typed metadata error, bytes discarded |
| Formal spec or custom verifier | After the built-in checks, still in memory | Typed verifier error, bytes discarded |

```ts
import { verifyBuffer, verifyStream } from "@adaptate/core/verify";

const checked = await verifyBuffer(bytes, {
  hash: { value: expectedSha256 },
  size: bytes.byteLength,
});

if (!checked.ok) {
  checked.failures;
}

const streamed = await verifyStream(chunks, {
  hash: { algorithm: "SHA-256", value: expectedSha256 },
});
```

`@adaptate/core/verify` is part of zero-dependency `@adaptate/core`. For a large or batched buffer, `@adaptate/accel` can size-route the same kind of check; see [Acceleration](accel.md). Pair this with [`makeFeed`](v3.md) when the bytes arrive as a stream.

This page is under Advanced because the hooks check untrusted buffers in memory, not ordinary fields on a small tool-call chunk. If a hook cannot decide, it does not write.


# Migration 2.4

Source: docs/migration-2.4.md

---
title: "Migration 2.4"
description: "YAML and the ref parser became optional peers between 2.3 and 2.4."
answer: "Version 2.4 of @adaptate/utils makes js-yaml and the JSON Schema ref parser optional peers. Install js-yaml only to parse YAML, and the ref parser only for remote or file $ref pointers."
faq:
  - question: "Do I need to change code to upgrade?"
    answer: "No code change is needed. Install the optional peers your app uses."
  - question: "What is new in @adaptate/core?"
    answer: "@adaptate/core/standard validates a Standard Schema, and @adaptate/core/effect runs checks in Effect."
---

# Migration 2.3 → 2.4

Published 2.3.0 of `@adaptate/utils` depended on `@apidevtools/json-schema-ref-parser@^15.3.5` and `js-yaml@^4.1.1`.

2.4 makes both optional:

- Install `js-yaml@^5.5.0` if you parse YAML.
- Install `@apidevtools/json-schema-ref-parser@^16.0.8` if you resolve remote or file `$ref`s.
- In-document `$ref`s stay on the local resolver. JSON specs need neither package.

[#51](https://github.com/p10ns11y/adaptate/pull/51) moved those packages from parser 15 and js-yaml 4 to parser 16 and js-yaml 5, and dropped `@types/js-yaml` because js-yaml 5 ships its types. The Zod peer stays `^3.25.0 || ^4.0.0`. `@adaptate/core` still has no runtime dependencies.

`@adaptate/core/standard` validates a Standard Schema (`~standard.validate`) and adds no dependency. The test uses a transformed Zod schema and a hand-written schema ([`standard.test.ts`](../packages/core/src/__tests__/standard.test.ts)).

`@adaptate/core/effect` is new. Install `effect@^4.0.0` only if you import it. `final(text)` and `final(text, configName)` are in [Effect](effect.md).


# Migration 3.0

Source: docs/migration-3.0.md

---
title: "Migration 3.0"
description: "v3 is additive: makeFeed, @adaptate/core/verify, and optional acceleration packages, with the default install still zero-dep."
answer: "v3 is additive for 2.4 callers. makeFeed is optional on fromAsyncIterableSteps and parseStream, @adaptate/core/verify is a new subpath, and the acceleration packages are optional Advanced installs. adaptate and @adaptate/core stay zero-dependency aside from the zod peer."
faq:
  - question: "Do I need to change code to upgrade?"
    answer: "No. Existing imports and the default feed stay the same. Adopt makeFeed, @adaptate/core/verify, or an acceleration package only when you need them."
  - question: "Does the default install gain dependencies?"
    answer: "No. adaptate and @adaptate/core still have no runtime dependencies. Acceleration packages are separate optional installs."
---

# Migration 2.4 → 3.0

v3 is backward compatible for 2.4 callers. Published package versions stay on the 2.4 line until the v3 release; the APIs below are already in this repository as additive entries.

What is new, all optional:

- `makeFeed` on `fromAsyncIterableSteps` and `parseStream`. Omit it and the default tracked feed is used. `openPath` and `tailOpen` stay on the step. See [v3 feeds](v3.md).
- `@adaptate/core/verify` for fail-closed in-memory checks (issue 84): `hashBuffer`, `verifyBuffer`, `verifyStream`. This is a new subpath of zero-dependency `@adaptate/core`. See [Runtime verification](verification.md).
- Optional Advanced packages `@adaptate/accel`, `@adaptate/wasm`, and `@adaptate/native`, plus the Rust core they wrap. Install them only for large buffers, multi-MB verification, or a host embed. They are not peers of `@adaptate/core` and they do not load from the default install. See [Acceleration](accel.md).

What does not change:

- The default install remains `adaptate` / `@adaptate/core` plus the `zod` peer, with `effect`, `js-yaml`, and the ref parser still optional as in [Migration 2.4](migration-2.4.md).
- Existing subpaths (`/stream`, `/stream-incremental`, `/standard`, `/effect`, `/result`) keep their current imports.
- Small streaming chunks should stay on the JS parser. Measured SHA-256 at 1 KiB, 32 KiB, and 2 MiB was faster in JS than WASM or native on the Track 2 real-binary run.

If you already consume 2.4, upgrade when the v3 npm release ships, then add only the new imports you want. No rewrite is required.


# Development

Source: docs/development.md

---
title: "Development"
description: "Install, test, and build this repository with pnpm."
answer: "Tested with pnpm 11.1.1 and Node 24.22.1 (pinned in package.json and pnpm-lock.yaml) on 2026-11-23. Run pnpm install, pnpm lint, pnpm test, and pnpm build. npm install at the repository root is not supported."
faq:
  - question: "Why not npm install?"
    answer: "npm does not apply the supply-chain settings in .npmrc and pnpm-workspace.yaml, and the tree can diverge from CI."
  - question: "How do I refresh the API reference?"
    answer: "Run pnpm build, then pnpm docs:api. The verify job fails when docs/api or llms.txt drift."
---

# Development

Tested with pnpm 11.1.1 and Node 24.22.1 (pinned, locked) on 2026-11-23. Root `package.json` sets `"packageManager": "pnpm@11.1.1"`. `.npmrc` and `pnpm-workspace.yaml` set lifecycle restrictions, store integrity, and the minimum release age. `npm install` at the repo root is unsupported: npm does not apply those settings, and the tree can diverge from CI.

`pnpm add` / `npm install` of the published `@adaptate/*` packages is how consumers install from the registry.

`pnpm docs:api` rewrites [docs/api](api/index.md) from the built `.d.ts` files, and rewrites `llms.txt` and `llms-full.txt`. Run it after `pnpm build`. The verify job fails when those files drift.

Engines: the repo and `@adaptate/core` require Node `>=24`. `@adaptate/utils` declares Node `>=20`.

```sh
pnpm install
pnpm lint
pnpm test          # check-types, then vitest run --coverage
pnpm test:watch
pnpm build         # turbo run build
pnpm typecheck
```

Agent procedures: [AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md), [skills/](../skills/). Dev container: [.devcontainer/README.md](../.devcontainer/README.md).

License: MIT.

# Function: validatePartialAgainstConfigs()

title: "Function: validatePartialAgainstConfigs()"

# Type Alias: Config\<T\>

Source: docs/api/core/index/type-aliases/Config.md

---
title: "Type Alias: Config\\<T\\>"
description: "Type-safe configuration for `transformSchema` and conditional transformers."
---

# Type Alias: Config\<T\>

> **Config**\<`T`\> = `boolean` \| `unknown` *extends* `T` ? `object` & `object` : `T` *extends* readonly infer U[] ? `object` : `T` *extends* `object` ? `{ [K in keyof T]?: Config<T[K]> }` : `never`

Type-safe configuration for `transformSchema` and conditional transformers.

## High-value use cases this type enables:
- Full autocomplete for every field path in your schema
- Compile-time errors for typos or non-existent fields
- Natural support for deeply nested objects
- Special `'*'` syntax for array element configuration
- `true` = make required, `false` = keep optional (or omit)

## Type Parameters

### T

`T` = `unknown`

## Example

```ts
const config = {
  name: true,
  address: { city: true, country: false },
  tags: { '*': true },
} satisfies Config<z.infer<typeof mySchema>>;
```

# Type Alias: StreamStep\<T, P\>

Source: docs/api/core/result/type-aliases/StreamStep.md

---
title: "Type Alias: StreamStep\\<T, P\\>"
description: "One `parseStream` step. `openPath` holds the keys from the root to the deepest open value. A value off `openPath` is final unless the document repeats a key on that path later (..."
---

# Type Alias: StreamStep\<T, P\>

> **StreamStep**\<`T`, `P`\> = \{ `done`: `false`; `openPath?`: [`JsonPath`](../../stream-incremental/type-aliases/JsonPath.md); `result`: [`Result`](Result.md)\<`P`\>; `tailOpen?`: `boolean`; \} \| \{ `done`: `true`; `openPath?`: [`JsonPath`](../../stream-incremental/type-aliases/JsonPath.md); `result`: [`Result`](Result.md)\<`T`\>; `tailOpen?`: `boolean`; \}

One `parseStream` step. `openPath` holds the keys from the root to the deepest open
value. A value off `openPath` is final unless the document repeats a key on that path later
(`JSON.parse` lets the last duplicate win). A partial step whose partial schema fails
has no `result.value`, so no path on it is settled.

## Type Parameters

### T

`T`

### P

`P`

# Function: isSettled()

Source: docs/api/core/stream-incremental/functions/isSettled.md

---
title: "Function: isSettled()"
description: "True when `path` holds a value that later steps will not change, unless the document repeats a key on that path."
---

# Function: isSettled()

> **isSettled**(`step`, `path`): `boolean`

True when `path` holds a value that later steps will not change, unless the document repeats a key on that path.

Array steps take integer index keys and object steps take string keys, as in `openPath`.
A value off `openPath` is final unless the document repeats a key on that path later
(`JSON.parse` lets the last duplicate win). A partial step whose partial schema
fails has no `result.value`, so no path on it is settled.

## Parameters

### step

[`JsonStreamStep`](../type-aliases/JsonStreamStep.md) \| \{ `done`: `boolean`; `openPath?`: [`JsonPath`](../type-aliases/JsonPath.md); `result`: \{ `ok`: `boolean`; `value?`: `unknown`; \}; \}

### path

[`JsonPath`](../type-aliases/JsonPath.md)

## Returns

`boolean`

# Function: openAPISchemaToZod()

---

# Function: openAPISchemaToZod()

> **openAPISchemaToZod**(`schema`, `propertyKey?`, `required?`): `ZodType`

Converts an OpenAPI / JSON Schema object to a Zod schema.
Supports a wide range of features for feature-completeness:
- Primitives: string, number, integer, boolean
- Complex: object, array, enum
- Validations: min/max length, min/max, pattern, format (email, uuid, url, datetime, etc.)
- Combinators: allOf (intersection), anyOf/oneOf (union)
- Nullable
- Proper required field handling

Note: $ref should be pre-resolved by getDereferencedOpenAPIDocument.

## Parameters

### schema

`any`

### propertyKey?

`string`

### required?

`string`[]

## Returns

`ZodType`


# Function: zodToOpenAPISchema()

Source: docs/api/utils/openapi/functions/zodToOpenAPISchema.md

---
title: "Function: zodToOpenAPISchema()"
description: "Converts a Zod schema to an OpenAPI / JSON Schema compatible object. Now feature-complete with: - Proper `required` array for objects (excludes .optional() fields) - Support for..."
---

# Function: zodToOpenAPISchema()

> **zodToOpenAPISchema**(`zodSchema`): `any`

Converts a Zod schema to an OpenAPI / JSON Schema compatible object.
Now feature-complete with:
- Proper `required` array for objects (excludes .optional() fields)
- Support for .nullable()
- String validations: minLength, maxLength, pattern, format
- Number validations: minimum, maximum, exclusive*, multipleOf, integer
- Array minItems / maxItems
- Enum support
- Union / anyOf
- Description from .describe()
- Zod 4 attached checks (`_zod.def.checks`) and legacy `_def.checks` where present

## Parameters

### zodSchema

`ZodType`

## Returns

`any`
